title: Solo UE5 action RPG: AI for the models and code, the music and sound by me. Anyone cracked AI-assisted animation?
author: AuralithDev
selftext:
I'm building Auralith, a single-player sci-fi action RPG, solo in Unreal Engine 5. Every weapon and all five armor sets started as image-to-3D generations: I make concept images locally with FLUX.1, some with chatGPT, and Meshy turns them into models. What surprised me is how little of the work that saves on armor, which I've been rigging in Blender.



I have a degree and 14 years of experience in pro audio, plus a Computer Science degree I earned during the pandemic. I make all the music myself, and the sound effects are mostly my own recordings, all routed through Wwise into UE5.



On the code side, much of the game was written with AI coding assistants (Claude and Codex), with me directing, testing and playing. I've been able to get a lot more done recently by having models use automated tests that boot the game and UE5 with out me needing to constantly check every detail over and over again.



What isn't AI: the music is mine (I'm an audio engineer and musician). Sound effects come mostly from my own recordings (I'm learning more about Foley daily). My current animations are from licensed packs. Everything in the trailer is in-game footage. If anyone has found a workflow that works for creating your own 3D animations in an AI assisted way, I would be really curious to know what your workflow is.



The Kickstarter hasn't started yet; the pre-launch page is here if you'd like to hear when it opens: [https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/playauralith/auralith](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/playauralith/auralith)

comments.author: AuralithDev
comments.body: Thanks for the reply. I'm actually not paying for max credits. My AI credits are supplied by my employer to assist with me doing work as a full time lead software engineer... The only software engineer employed by the company. The extra tokens go towards my other projects, this being one of them and another (a personal safety app released on the apple app store to help people). That being said, I am interested if anyone has thought about using AI for animation purposes.

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body:
a lot of people have. there is even good results, with a lot of work like front/side videos of the creature and very strict llm to llm iteration control.

BUT it always was a lot of work. only worth it if you have something that is not "mainstream" like a person. or you realy want your unique animation style to be dominant and a main selling point. and then its probably equal work than doing them manually as a professional animator.
